notes.text: LANDING BLOCKER after bob-cli-3j.9 (do not close yet): completion::zsh_adapter::default_styles_use_green_headers fails when the runner exports NO_COLOR=1. Reproduced 2026-10-02 on master 712d277: cargo test --test cli completion::zsh_adapter::default_styles_use_green_headers exits failed and the stub prints `format '── %d ──'` with no %B%F{green}. env -u NO_COLOR makes that same test pass. no_color_uses_plain_header passed in the NO_COLOR=1 run. Cause: _bob.zsh sets the plain header when NO_COLOR is set, and run_stubbed inherits the process environment. Neither _bob.zsh nor default_styles_use_green_headers was changed by 8f01f33 or 712d277. Fix: in that test's pre script, unset NO_COLOR before _bob, then re-run the completion cli tests. The rest of the 3j.9 recheck is in the child close note. Eight phases are closed, there are no --epic-symbol entries, and there are no non-epic commits after 81b45eb besides the child epic's own two commits.

notes.author: bob-cli-3n.12.9.land
notes.text: DISCOVERED ISSUE (from bob-cli-3n.12.9 landing; proposed by bob-cli-3n.12.9.2 note #2 and bob-cli-3n.12.9.4 note #2): completion CLI tests flake under parallel cargo test. (a) completion::vault plugins_come_from_the_repo_checkout and task_sections_offer_exact_titles failed once with empty stdout under a parallel just test, passing alone and on rerun. Likely cause: tests/cli/completion/vault.rs complete() runs bob __complete with no BOB_COMPLETE_DEADLINE_MS, so the 150 ms COMPLETE_DEADLINE_MS vault-scan deadline (src/native/completion/mod.rs) expires under load and completion prints nothing by design. (b) completion::bash::bash_readline_inserts_what_bob_returned fails in a full parallel run, passing alone: the zpty READLINE_DRIVER relies on fixed sleep 0.3/0.5/1 delays and the same unset 150 ms deadline. Suggested fix: set a generous BOB_COMPLETE_DEADLINE_MS in the test helpers (keep the one test that pins the deadline), and make the zpty driver wait for output rather than sleep. These tests and the deadline come from this epic (eafe65c, 5a60bd8, 712d277), not from bob-cli-3n.12.9.

title: task-status-cycler: Alt+]/Alt+[ closing a task skips finalizeClosedTasks (no immediate Blocked-dependent recovery)
description:
In bob-plugins `plugins/task-status-cycler/main.js` (verified at bob-plugins `ede89d3`, task-status-cycler 1.19.0), the Alt+] / Alt+[ status cycle (`handleCycleCommand`, line ~8226) writes the new checkbox through `setActiveCheckboxStatus` and, when leaving `[?]`, runs `applyBlockedStatusRetirementInEditor`. It never calls `finalizeClosedTasks` (line ~6841), which is the hook every Ctrl+Enter close path uses (call sites ~8960, 9000, 9133, 9171, 9613, 9709) to:

1. recover Blocked `[?]` dependents whose last open `[dependsOn::]` target just closed (`recoverBlockedDependents`), and
2. retire closed-task references (strike `![[…]]` → `~~[[…]]~~`).

The cycle order is `? → ' ' → / → * → x → -`, so Alt+] from Next `[*]` lands on Done `[x]`, and Alt+[ from Blocked lands on Cancelled `[-]`. A prerequisite closed this way leaves its dependents `[?]` until the next `bob task-status-hooks` run (every 15 minutes on the MacBook), while the same close through Ctrl+Enter recovers them immediately. A code survey suggests the counted and transcluded cycle paths (around lines 8605, 8708–8746, 9254, and `cycleResolvedTranscludedTaskLink`) have the same gap; confirm before changing them.

Suggested fix: when a cycle (bare, counted, or transcluded-target) moves a task into a DONE or CANCELLED type, collect the closed identities and call `finalizeClosedTasks` exactly as the Ctrl+Enter paths do. Check the README row and docs/task-status-hooks.md ("Ctrl+Enter recovery in the Task Status Cycler plugin is intentionally narrower and immediate") first, in case cycling was deliberately left out of immediate recovery. If it was, record that decision in the README instead.

task_type_fields.impact: A dependent task looks Blocked for up to 15 minutes after its last prerequisite is closed by cycling; closed-task embeds are not retired until the hooks run. Low severity: the hooks backstop it.
task_type_fields.location: bob-plugins plugins/task-status-cycler/main.js handleCycleCommand (~8226) → setActiveCheckboxStatus; missing finalizeClosedTasks (~6841)
task_type_fields.repro: In Obsidian, give task B [id:: x__b] ^b and task A [dependsOn:: x__b] status [?]. Put the cursor on B (status [*]) and press Alt+]; B becomes [x]. A stays [?] until bob task-status-hooks runs. Repeat with Ctrl+Enter on B: A is reopened to [ ] immediately.

creation_reason: Found while researching task dependency links: closing a prerequisite by status cycling, unlike Ctrl+Enter, leaves its dependents Blocked until the next hooks run, an inconsistency between two close gestures.

title: Task dependency links: one Depends-On line, a vault-wide Ctrl+Shift+P picker, and live chips
description: A task's prerequisites live as plain task dependency links on one managed `⛓️ **DEPENDS ON:**` first-child line. That line is the source of truth, and the `[dependsOn::]` / `[id::]` fields are derived from it. Ctrl+Shift+P adds and removes prerequisites by fuzzy-searching every open task in the vault. bob-ledger-tools draws each link as a live status chip. The vault no longer uses transcluded dependency bullets. The glossary, docs, and decision records describe the new contract.

title: ob lock_wait_behavior intermittently fails with Contended under parallel cargo test
description: Intermittent full-suite failure of native::ob::tests::lock_wait_behavior, proposed as a follow-up by bob-cli-3s.4. See the flake report below for the evidence and the suspected flock fork-inherited-fd mechanism.

task_type_fields.evidence:
Reported by phase bead bob-cli-3s.4 (epic bob-cli-3s, a structural split of capture_clip that does not touch src/native/ob.rs) on 2026-10-03: during full-suite default-parallel `just all` / `cargo test` runs, `native::ob::tests::lock_wait_behavior` failed intermittently with a `Contended` lock error. It passed in isolation and sometimes under `--test-threads=4`. The fail rate was not measured; it appeared in at least one of several full-suite runs. The bob-cli-3s land run's own `just all` passed.

Suspected root cause (unconfirmed; the exact failing `expect` was not captured): `try_acquire_lock` uses an flock-style `try_lock_exclusive`, which belongs to the open file description. After the test's `drop(held)`, another lib test thread that is spawning a child process (many lib tests run `git` via `Command`) can still hold a fork-inherited duplicate of the lock fd until its `exec` closes it (CLOEXEC). During that window, the immediate `try_acquire_lock().expect("re-acquire lock")` sees `WouldBlock` and panics with `Contended`. The only `expect`s in this test that can surface `Contended` are "initial lock" and "re-acquire lock"; the waiter and zero-budget paths return `LockWaitError::Timeout` instead.

Check this before fixing. One option is to make the re-acquire tolerate a brief inherited-fd window (for example, `acquire_lock_waiting` with a short budget) without weakening the callback-count assertions. Do not serialize the whole suite.

creation_reason: Proposed by bob-cli-3s.4 as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP during epic bob-cli-3s; the flake is in src/native/ob.rs, which the epic did not touch, so it is separate work.

title: Stage ranker 16 ms perf assertion flakes under parallel npm test load
description:
Repo: bob-plugins (linked), master 9c271e1. The test's own body was last changed in da7cce4.

- `npm test` failed in 2 of 2 full-suite runs during the bob-cli-3v landing. One measured 16.17 ms with `cargo test` running at the same time. The other measured 28.57 ms with the host at load average ~8.9 on 16 cores. Everything else passed (1575/1576).
- `node --test scripts/test-navigation-dependencies-stage.cjs` passed on its own (10.34 ms, 62/62).
- bob-cli-3v.2 saw the same thing earlier: 16.03 ms in the full suite, 6 ms on its own, in a file it did not touch. bob-cli-3v.5 and bob-cli-3v.6 later got green full-suite runs.

Root cause: the test times one cold `dependencyStageRank(pool, "synthetic cash")` call with `process.hrtime` and asserts it is under 16 ms. `node --test` runs the test files in parallel, so JIT warm-up and CPU contention from other files and other agents decide the result. The ranker code itself is not the cause. Fix idea: warm the ranker up first, then take the min or median of several runs. Or move the timing budget behind an opt-in perf env var so normal `npm test` checks only correctness.

title: Two bob-mac-capture close tests fail once the suite compiles (masked by bob-cli-3m)
description:
Found by bob-cli-3u.land (epic bob-cli-3u landing; not proposed by a phase) while running the bob-mac-capture suite on a macOS 26 / Swift 6.3.2 **Command Line Tools-only** Mac. That Mac has no XCTest.framework, so the suite ran under a throwaway XCTest stand-in: assertions, XCTUnwrap and XCTSkip, plus a generated runner `dlopen`ed from the SwiftPM test bundle. The stand-in was never committed. The same two failures appear identically at pre-epic 68ed00d and at 680e17f plus the bob-cli-3u landing fixes. Under the stand-in, 622 CaptureCore, 16 install-helper and ~500 panel tests otherwise pass.

CI never reaches them: bob-cli-3m's compile error at `CapturePanelModelTests.swift:2024` breaks the Test step first. These failures will surface as soon as bob-cli-3m lands, so fix them together or right after it.

1. `Tests/CaptureCoreTests/CapturePomodoroClosePresentationTests.swift::testShortAliasPreviewShowsDefaultTaskOne` (from aa1e73a) fails at line 1625, `XCTAssertTrue(parked.accessibilityLabel.contains("Parked"))`.
   - Root cause: `CapturePomodoroClosePresentation.swift:549` (1056569) builds `"Task N, <text>, <transition>, parked, not carried to the next Pomodoro"`, with a lowercase `parked`, and `String.contains` is case-sensitive.
   - Fix: decide which spelling VoiceOver should read (the row's visible badge is `"Parked · not carried"`), then align the test or the label.
   - Re-check the rest of that test after the fix, because XCTest continues after the first failure.
2. `Tests/BobMacCaptureTests/CapturePanelModelTests.swift::testMixedDraftSurfacesBobDiagnostic` (from 68ed00d) times out at line 2628 waiting for `previewState == .failed`.
   - fake-bob answers `capture-parse` for `=x\n- foo\n- 2 bar` with `Tests/Fixtures/pomodoro-close-parse-log-mixed.json`. That payload is `ok: true`, mode `pomodoro_close`, `needs: []`, plus an error-severity `invalid_pomodoro_close` diagnostic.
   - The panel model apparently does not turn that diagnostic into `.failed`. Either it proceeds to a `capture --dry-run` that fake-bob has no branch for, or it ignores error diagnostics.
   - Fix: determine which, and fix the model if real Bob behaves this way, or the fixture/fake-bob if not.

Verify with the real macOS CI run (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), not only locally.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Both fail identically at pre-epic 68ed00d and at 680e17f with landing fixes. The first is a deterministic case-sensitive string assertion: the source label says 'parked' and the test expects 'Parked'. The second times out on the same fixed fake-bob payload every run.

plus_one_evidence.note: Independent code read (bob-plugins master 79d5975, nav 1.71.0): confirmed showRefreshValueStage (main.js:24971) passes footerHints: ["↵ apply · esc back"] (a string) and FilteredPickerModal.renderFooter calls hint.keys.forEach. Wider impact than the original report: the approved-decay card's Less-often picker path (openFreshnessDecayLessOftenPicker, main.js ~35303-35394, used when lessOften.mode === "picker", i.e. 90+ day intervals) calls picker.showRefreshValueStage(...), overrides items/title/getSubtitle/openItem but NOT footerHints, then picker.open(); onOpen -> renderAll -> renderFooter throws, so the surrounding catch shows 'Could not update task; no tasks were updated' and the preset list never renders. Timing: docs/freshness.md (review outcomes) documents 'see it less often (Ctrl+Shift+P -> refresh -> 14 / 30 / 90)' for the trial that starts 2026-10-05, and the decision card activates 2026-10-19, so the fix should land before 10-05. Vault re-check: still 0 [refresh:: N] fields.

task_type_fields.impact: The Ctrl+Shift+P "Refresh every" row (the documented "see it less often" review outcome in docs/freshness.md) likely cannot be used: the value stage paints stale rows and a blind ↵ can write a 2-day refresh the user never saw. Fix: pass `[{ keys: ["↵"], label: "Apply" }, { keys: ["esc"], label: "Dismiss" }]` (Esc closes the picker; it does not go back) and harden renderFooter to skip or stringify non-object hints; add a DOM-stub test that opens the stage through renderAll.
task_type_fields.location: bob-plugins plugins/bob-navigation-hotkeys/main.js BulletPropertyPickerModal.showRefreshValueStage (footerHints) + FilteredPickerModal.renderFooter
task_type_fields.repro: By code reading (bob-plugins master 79d5975): BulletPropertyPickerModal.showRefreshValueStage (plugins/bob-navigation-hotkeys/main.js:24955) passes `footerHints: ["↵ apply · esc back"]` — a bare string — where every other stage passes `{ keys: [...], label }` objects. FilteredPickerModal.renderFooter (main.js:~16068) does `hint.keys.forEach(...)` for each hint, so a string hint throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'forEach')`. renderAll() calls renderFooter() BEFORE renderResults(), so in a real (DOM-backed) modal: Ctrl+Shift+P → "Refresh every" row → ↵ should throw, leaving the stage-one property rows painted while applyOptions() has already pointed this.items/visibleItems at the refresh presets. A following ↵ would then apply the first preset (2 days) that is not on screen. Minimal logic check: `node -e 'const hints=["↵ apply · esc back"]; hints.forEach((h)=>h.keys.forEach(()=>{}))'` throws. The class is not exported and the node tests never open a DOM-backed modal (resultsEl is null, so renderAll is skipped), which is why scripts/test-navigation-stamps.cjs does not catch it. Corroborating signal: the Bob vault contains zero `[refresh:: N]` fields although the row shipped in nav 1.44.0. Confirm in Obsidian before fixing.

creation_reason: Found while researching the Ctrl+Shift+P panel redesign: the refresh stage's footer hint has the wrong shape, which likely breaks the Refresh every row in real Obsidian and may explain why the vault has zero refresh fields.

title: Priority bullet property that rolls a scheduled date
description: The Ctrl+Shift+P bullet-property picker offers a `priority` property whose P2/P3/P4 levels each write a random `scheduled` date drawn from a per-level day range configured in bob/config.yml, and the `scheduled` date picker offers a visually distinct re-rollable date suggestion whenever the current task already has a priority.

notes.author: bob-cli-e.land
notes.text:
Land verification. Read every child note and the epic's commits in both repos, then the source: config validation (levels label/value uniqueness, bracket/'::'/newline rejection, non-negative integer day ranges, min<=max, 'levels' rejected on non-priority entries, cross-entry 'schedules' must name another date property) in validateBulletPropertyConfig/normalizeBulletPriorityProperty; rollPriorityScheduledDate inclusive with a clamp for random()===1; priority value rows in config order with label/value/window/searchText/current; signal-high chrome, 'Filter priorities', 'priority levels', level-aware subtitles and currentLabel resolved through levelsByValue; setInlineBulletPropertyValues extracted and reused by setBulletPropertyValue with Blocked/recovery intact; ^prj routing that writes priority inline and the rolled date to frontmatter under one notice; counted 'set-priority' with a per-target roll map, per-target Blocked/recovery, project-frontmatter branch and stale-session guard; pinned dices-icon priority-roll item with Ctrl+R re-roll, footer hint only when a roll exists, and counted common-priority gating; styles, manifest 1.14.x, README row, docs/projects.md. Verified chezmoi source and deployed ~/.config/bob/config.yml carry the priority entry and match, and the vault plugin files are byte-identical to source (cmp).

Integration: no commits landed in bob-cli or bob-plugins after this epic's first commit (2026-08-03 04:15), and none landed concurrently (last non-epic commits 2026-08-01 and 2026-07-31). Both repos are on master with no other branches or PRs, so there was nothing to re-integrate. Checked adjacent pre-existing surfaces for conflict or duplication: the legacy numeric [p:: N] project/highlights field uses a distinct key and does not collide with [priority:: ...]; bob-cli's Rust Tasks parser already accepts the written values; README.md, docs/dataview.md and docs/task-status-hooks.md do not enumerate picker properties, so nothing went stale.

Defect found and fixed as epic work (bob-plugins ed6386f, navigation-hotkeys 1.14.1): the single-task writer upserted priority and then scheduled onto the live line, so a task that already carried [scheduled:: ...] had that field replaced in place and ended with [priority:: ...] rightmost - the opposite of the counted writer, which rebuilds the date after the priority. Harmless while every level value is a Tasks priority name, but the plan documents changing 'value:' in config as the supported way to store a literal P2, and under that config the old order would have hidden scheduled/id/dependsOn from every right-to-left trailing-field parse. Inline writes now accept reorderPropertyNames and drop the schedules field before writing the priority; both writers assert the exact resulting line shape. npm test 268/268, npm run validate 6/6, git diff --check clean, re-synced to the vault and re-verified byte parity.

No PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP entries were recorded on any child bead, so no task beads were proposed. 'just symvision' is not available in this project (no recipe in the justfile, no symvision binary), so no epic-symbol whitelist sweep was possible; no whitelist entries naming this epic exist in the repo. Obsidian plugin reload is still required to pick up 1.14.1.

title: bob-navigation-hotkeys: plain scheduled-property picker write doesn't thread picker baseDate as today for Blocked marking
close_reason: Let's let this slide for now.
description:
In BulletPropertyPickerModal.applySelectedValue (plugins/bob-navigation-hotkeys/main.js, bob-plugins repo), the generic (non-priority, non-project-frontmatter) branch calls this.plugin.setBulletPropertyValue(...) without a `today` option:

    return await this.plugin.setBulletPropertyValue(
      this.editor,
      this.cursor,
      this.selectedPropertyItem.property.name,
      item.value,
      {
        filePath: this.filePath,
        expectedLine: this.lineText,
        scheduleLog: options.scheduleLog,
      },
    );

setBulletPropertyValue forwards to setInlineBulletPropertyValues, whose blocking check falls back to `options.today instanceof Date ? ... : new Date()` -- i.e. real wall-clock time -- when deciding whether a chosen `scheduled` date is "future" and should mark the task Blocked ([?]).

This is inconsistent with the priority-level write path (setBulletPriorityValue), which explicitly threads `baseDate: this.valueBaseDate` through as `today` so Blocked-marking is reproducible relative to the picker's own fixed base date, not the real clock.

Effect: picking a plain scheduled date (including the pinned priority-roll suggestion row in the `scheduled` value stage, which also goes through this generic branch) produces Blocked-marking that silently depends on when the code actually runs, not on the picker's `valueBaseDate`. A fixture asserting a specific Blocked/[?'] vs unblocked/[ ] outcome for this path will start failing (or silently stop covering the intended case) as real time passes the fixture's hardcoded dates.

Found while implementing bob-cli's plan sase/repos/plans/202608/auto_schedule_reasons.md (deterministic schedule-log reasons for machine-rolled dates). A new test for the pinned priority-roll suggestion ("choosing a priority roll writes immediately with a deterministic reason instead of prompting", scripts/test-navigation-hotkeys.cjs) had to read the actual checkbox status at runtime via helpers.getObsidianTaskCheckboxStatus() instead of asserting a hardcoded [?'] or [ ], specifically to route around this wall-clock dependency -- the plan's own worked example assumed [?'] but the assertion only holds if the test happens to run before the rolled date, which is not guaranteed.

Suggested fix: thread `today: this.valueBaseDate` (falling back to a fresh Date the way the priority path already does) through applySelectedValue's generic property branch, matching the priority branch's existing pattern.

The link written to this commit may remain unavailable until the outbox is cleared.' The SASE_AGENT link in those commit messages therefore points at an agent page that may never materialize.

Not specific to one project. sase agent sync --check --json also shows the same class of quarantine diagnostic under project actstat: "publication request bbugyi200.athena.sase-js.9@9f51c7b86c58 retired as unpublishable: published agent page for 'bbugyi200.athena.sase-js.9' did not materialize during full sync; run 'sase agent sync --drop-retired' to drop it".

The tool names its own remedy: sase agent sync --drop-retired, which drops retired publication requests and reports how many were dropped and why. Scope: run it, confirm the outbox clears for every affected project, re-run a commit (or sase agent sync --check) to confirm the warning is gone, and confirm whether the affected commits' SASE_AGENT links now resolve or need a republish. Left unrun by agents so far because the flagless sync also drains publication retries, publishes commit-eligible hoods, and pushes across projects — a cross-cutting action outside any one phase's scope.

Proposed as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note by epic phase bead bob-cli-j.4, and re-observed by the bob-cli-j land agent on commit f59ab74.

Checked recent bob-mac-capture SASE_AGENT URLs, including f59ab74, and all returned HTTP 200; no republish needed.

notes.author: bob-cli-m.land
notes.text: LANDED. Verified both phases against their notes, the source, and real behavior. bob-cli-m.1 (commit 2d6b0af): capture_language.rs splits TEXT into physical lines, capture.rs renders authored children at the target's dominant indent, and assemble_capture_block orders parent -> authored children -> clip children -> schedule log. Confirmed end-to-end against temp vaults with a freshly built binary, not just from tests: a three-line draft whose child line carries '@work p:1' routed the whole capture, stripped both markers from the child text, and wrote the parent plus two-space-indented children and the schedule log in the documented order; --task-ref nesting put authored children one level under the captured sub-bullet; cross-line duplicate @route and non-bullet continuation prose both failed with precise diagnostics and no write. cargo test capture is green (221 unit + 126 CLI) and the bob-cli tree is clean at 7fa0658. bob-cli-m.2 (commit 727b05d) delivered Ctrl-J/Backspace and sub_bullets decoding but left three gaps, all fixed here in bob-mac-capture commit 3d99000: explicit Preview omitted clip.lines and schedule_log.lines (added CaptureCommandSuccess.previewBlockLines in CaptureCore, rendered by PreviewPane, so preview mirrors Bob's full block; live preview's --no-clip guarantee is unchanged); the router claimed Shift-Backspace despite the plain-Backspace-only contract (all modified Backspace now falls through to AppKit, and the test that asserted the wrong behavior was corrected); and the native edit paths had no coverage beyond their range helper (split into insertBulletNewlineInEditableTextView/deleteEmptyBulletRowInEditableTextView and covered for selection replacement, caret placement, first/middle/final placeholder rows, and pass-through for nonempty rows, ranged selections, noneditable views, and unrelated responders). All 11 new/changed tests pass on real macOS 26 CI (run 31819844188), which closes bob-cli-m.2's largest gap: its AppKit code was previously only reasoned about, never compiled or executed. CaptureCore also verified locally (70 tests, 3 failures identical to unmodified origin/master's 67-test baseline). INTEGRATION: post-start commits d5eaf97 (bob-cli-n.1 wikilink protocol) and 7fa0658 (clip.entries) already consume the line-aware model correctly — the wikilink scanner is line-based and capture-complete defers to capture_language::completion_field_at for line-scoped marker completion; in bob-mac-capture this work rebased onto 60ac163, 2d98f19 and 1d859d9, and the CaptureModelTests conflict with 60ac163 was resolved keeping both sides. FOLLOW-UP OUTCOMES: bob-cli-m.1's nightly shared-sync 'Text file busy' flake -> ready task bob-cli-o (filed by the prior land pass; not re-filed). bob-cli-m.2's missing clip/schedule-log preview -> fixed here rather than deferred, since the epic's own plan requires it. macOS CI is still red on master from four failures that all reproduce without this epic's changes (two pre-epic autosizing metrics, one AttributedString caret defect from bob-cli-n.2 that also reproduces on Linux, and one varying completion case) -> recorded as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on active epic bob-cli-n rather than a new task, because it blocks bob-cli-n.3's release gate and is caused by that epic's work. notes.text: Implemented in the linked bob-mac-capture repo per capture_authored_sub_bullets.md: (1) CaptureCore/CaptureModels.swift decodes additive sub_bullets on CaptureParseResponse and CaptureCommandSuccess, tolerant of the key being absent; (2) CaptureKeyCommandRouter adds insertBulletNewline (Ctrl-J, keyCode 38+control) and deleteBackward (plain Backspace) commands; (3) CapturePanelController handles them via the first-responder NSTextView's native insertText(_:replacementRange:), inserting '\n- ' for Ctrl-J and, for Backspace, deleting an exactly '- ' placeholder row plus its preceding newline (or just the row on the first line) via the new emptyBulletRowDeletionRange(in:) helper; (4) CapturePanelView derives the real caret UTF-8 byte offset from AttributedTextSelection.indices(in:) instead of always assuming end-of-draft, and PreviewPane renders task_line followed by every sub_bullets line in source order/indentation (no more 2-line cap), scrolling internally past 140pt when bullets are present; (5) README's keyboard table, multiline example, and live-preview docs updated; the obsolete 'multiline is whitespace-normalized' claim is removed. The BobMacCapture/BobMacCaptureTests target (Ctrl-J, Backspace, caret-offset, preview rendering) cannot compile on Linux (no AppKit) per this repo's own design note and the swift-toolchain-on-athena memory; those changes and their new router/controller tests are implemented and reasoned through carefully (cross-checked the newer AttributedTextSelection/AttributedString.Index API against WWDC25 sources) but require the repository's macOS CI and a manual pass on a Mac, as the plan itself mandates. title: Future-Pomodoro-link cleanup leaves a dangling trailing newline when the pruned bullet is the file's last line
close_reason: Stale task bead swept from triage.
description:
Discovered while implementing the plan activate_future_scheduled_pomodoro_links.md
(bob-plugins repo, plugins/block-id-prompt/main.js).

listItemSubtreeEdit() (used by planFuturePomodoroLinkCleanup(), called from
completeTaskSourceLink() to prune duplicate future-Pomodoro links) computes the removed
span as [start-of-removed-line, start-of-next-line-or-content.length). This correctly
merges surrounding content when the removed bullet is in the middle of the file, but
when the removed bullet IS the file's last line (no trailing newline after it), the
newline that separated it from the PREVIOUS line is left untouched and nothing follows
to reconnect to, so the file gains a trailing newline it never had.

Repro: a note ending in (no trailing newline)
  - [ ] Later ()
    - [[Alpha#^ship]]
where "[[Alpha#^ship]]" is a dedicated duplicate-link bullet that
planFuturePomodoroLinkCleanup prunes as part of completing a task-picker link elsewhere
in the same Pomodoros section. After pruning, the file ends with

title: Remove Swift 6 Sendable warnings from Bob Mac Capture core
description: Proposed by phase bead bob-cli-t.2 during epic verification. On bob-mac-capture master dff08a7, swift build --target CaptureCore succeeds but reports two concurrency diagnostics that become Swift 6 errors: CaptureTargetsCache.swift:39 converts Date.init to an @Sendable closure, and BobProcessClient.swift:189 captures non-Sendable DispatchWorkItem in an @Sendable termination handler. Replace both with race-safe Sendable-compatible designs, add focused tests for injected time and timeout cancellation and one-shot continuation behavior, and verify the CaptureCore build no longer emits either diagnostic.

notes.author: bob-cli-w
notes.text: Fixed both Swift 6 Sendable diagnostics in bob-mac-capture CaptureCore (dff08a7 baseline): CaptureTargetsCache.swift:39 now defaults now: to a { Date() } closure literal instead of the bare Date.init reference; BobProcessClient.swift's timeoutWorkItem is now nonisolated(unsafe) (DispatchWorkItem.cancel() is documented thread-safe) so it can be captured from the @Sendable process.terminationHandler. Added 3 focused regression tests in BobProcessClientTests.swift: testRefreshUsesInjectedClockAndPreservesItAcrossFailure and testRefreshDefaultsToTheSystemClockWhenNoTimeIsInjected cover the injected-time default; testRepeatedTimeoutRacesResumeTheContinuationExactlyOnce runs the timeout-vs-termination-handler race 10x to guard the one-shot continuation behavior. Verified: swift build --target CaptureCore is clean (0 warnings, previously 2); swift build --target CaptureCoreTests compiles the new/existing tests with no errors. Could not execute swift test in this Linux SASE workspace since BobMacCaptureTests transitively depends on AppKit (repo is macOS 26 + Xcode-only per README/CI); actual test execution requires the macos-26 GitHub Actions runner. Changes are uncommitted in the bob-mac-capture linked repo checkout, left for review/commit.

title: Persist the Bob Mac Capture retained live draft across restarts
close_reason: I'm pretty sure we already did this.
description:
## Feature proposal

Persist the Bob Mac Capture retained live draft so Escape / failed-capture text survives Quit, Restart, crash, and logout.

After https://github.com/bobs-org/bob-mac-capture/pull/1, Control-C canceled drafts write through to `~/Library/Application Support/org.bobs.bob-mac-capture/canceled-draft-stash.json`. The in-editor live draft does not. `CapturePanelModel` still keeps it only in memory (`attributedDraft` / `plainDraft`, plus presentation state such as `errorMessage` and `statusText`). `prepareForRetainedClose()` / `closeRetainingDraft()` set `"Draft retained"` and dismiss the panel; `prepareForPresentation()` reopens that in-memory draft on the next hotkey. `AppDelegate` constructs a fresh `CapturePanelModel` on every launch, so the retained draft is gone after any process exit.

This is a different store from the canceled-draft stash: one current draft (not a bounded newest-first list), restored automatically on next panel open rather than through Control-S, and discarded by **Discard** / Control-C / successful capture rather than by Clear Stash. The approved persist-stash plan named this as out of scope and asked for a follow-up task bead rather than folding it into that PR.

### Evidence

- `Sources/BobMacCapture/CapturePanelModel.swift` — `prepareForRetainedClose()`, `closeRetainingDraft()`, `prepareForPresentation()`, and `discardDraft()` operate only on in-memory published state. There is no encode, decode, or file I/O.
- Tests `testEscapeClosesOnceAndRetainsNonemptyDraft` and `testEscapeDismissesCompletionBeforeClosingPanel` assert in-process retention only.
- PR-branch README Privacy still says captured text lives only in the panel's in-memory draft (plus the new on-disk stash for Control-C). A live-draft persist would be a second documented-guarantee change, same class of README/Settings rewrite the stash work required.

### Suggested shape (not a plan)

Mirror the stash store: Foundation-only CaptureCore JSON file under the same 0700 Application Support directory, write-through on retain/discard/success, delete the file when the live draft is empty, metadata-only errors, never interpolate draft text. Do not persist completion candidates, preview payloads, or diagnostics that are not needed to reopen the editor exactly as left. Confirm with the owner whether a failed capture's `errorMessage` should survive relaunch.

Work is in the `bob-mac-capture` linked repo. Linux can type-check CaptureCore only; macOS CI is the real gate.

Plan that scoped this out: `plan:202608/persist_canceled_draft_stash.md`.

notes.text: RELATED: bob-cli-q — drag-and-drop paste also edits CapturePanelModel / the capture editor; a live-draft persist that writes on every text change could collide with that change if both land together.

notes.author: 07p--1
notes.text: RELATED: bob-cli-r — large-paste policy also lives on the capture editor draft path; persist-on-every-keystroke vs persist-on-retain would interact with any size ceiling that bead adds.

notes.text: CONTEXT: persist-canceled-draft-stash shipped in https://github.com/bobs-org/bob-mac-capture/pull/1 (3bb1691); CI run 32262048348 is green. That PR persists Control-C stash only. This bead is the live-draft follow-up the plan scoped out.

task_type_fields.proposal: Persist the Bob Mac Capture in-editor retained live draft (Escape / failed capture) across Quit, Restart, crash, and logout. This is a single-draft store restored on the next panel open, not the Control-C canceled-draft stash.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The approved persist-canceled-draft-stash plan (and PR bobs-org/bob-mac-capture#1) explicitly left this out: it is a different store with different semantics (one current draft, not a bounded list; auto-restore on panel open, not Control-S). The user asked about the stash. Do not fold this into that PR.
